result_text:
OpenAPI resource templates now build their requests through the route's parameter mapping, like OpenAPI tools do. I ran four of the five read scenarios against a mock transport, and each produced the expected URL. Because my client set default query params and cookies, every URL also carried `?api-version=1`, and the `cookie` header was `session=abc` in each case.

- **Encoding:** `..%2F..%2Fadmin%2Fsecret` was requested as `.../users/%2E%2E%2F%2E%2E%2Fadmin%2Fsecret`.
- **Unmatched query string:** `resource://get_user/alice?admin=true` requested `.../users/alice`.
- **Hyphenated name:** `/users/{user-id}` read as `resource://get_user/abc` requested `.../users/abc`.
- **Query-name collision:** `id` in both path and query read as `resource://get_user/abc` requested `.../users/abc`.
- **Not exercised:** the `id__path` body-collision case and the three-location `id` schema check in `_combine_schemas_and_map_params`. I didn't write tests for either.

Of the 308 OpenAPI tests, 305 passed. Three performance tests failed in the parallel run. `test_github_api_schema_performance` also fails with my changes stashed, so it fails without them. I didn't check the other two on a clean tree. `test_memory_efficiency` passed when re-run on its own, but I didn't re-run `test_medium_schema_performance`.

- **`schemas.py`:** `_combine_schemas_and_map_params` now suffixes any parameter name that appears in more than one non-body location (`id__path`, `id__query`, `id__header`), as well as body collisions.
- **`components.py`:** `OpenAPIResource` takes `arguments: dict[str, Any] | None = None`. On read, it builds the request with the director. It then runs it through `client.build_request`, so the client's default params, cookies and headers apply, and MCP request headers go on top.
